title: wardenby affiliate transaction certification revision
instruction:
You are the senior regulatory accountant at Lanternwood Supply supporting Wardenby Utilities’ annual affiliate-transaction compliance filing, which controller Ragnhild Hendricks must sign next Friday and commission auditor Mateo Marchetti may use to decide whether to open a targeted audit. Revise the certification exhibit after Ragnhild’s review of the draft: she said it read like a tutorial, blurred management representations with accounting conclusions, did not explain the year-over-year movement, and implied audit assurance we did not perform. The exhibit must still make sense to an executive signer who does not work with affiliate accounting, while remaining concise enough for a specialist reviewer. Cover the year ended 31 December 2025 against 2024. Recorded affiliate transactions were $25.0 million and $23.1 million, respectively: Customer Operations $7.4 million versus $7.0 million, Shared IT $5.8 million versus $5.3 million, Fleet $4.2 million versus $4.1 million, and Engineering $7.6 million versus $6.7 million. Engineering’s increase reflects its peak-demand allocation model; its owner represented that the model was applied consistently, but accounting did not validate the model design or its operating inputs. The logs also net stale affiliate receivables against payables even though Wardenby’s manual prohibits offsetting: 2025 contains $0.78 million receivable and $0.47 million payable, shown as a $0.31 million net balance, compared with $0.18 million receivable and $0.085 million payable, shown as $0.095 million net, in 2024. Last cycle’s audit found late quarterly reconciliations and missing review evidence. The 2025 reconciliations were completed on time, but the Fleet second-quarter review is undated. The commission form expects one signing position, while unresolved matters must not be hidden or overstated. Present the facts without proposing remediation or management action, use no invented amounts or unsupported assurance language, and omit account-level identifiers. Produce a signature-ready exhibit of no more than two pages as `affiliate_transaction_certification_exhibit.docx`, written into the top level of the working directory using exactly that filename. Give Ragnhild exactly one defensible certification position—unqualified, qualified, or not supportable—and end on that decision rather than a next-steps list.

---

Write your finished work to the **top level of the current working directory**, using exactly these filenames:

- `affiliate_transaction_certification_exhibit.docx` — A two-page-or-shorter, signature-ready affiliate-transaction compliance certification exhibit comparing 2025 with 2024 and stating one defensible certification position. (Place the file at the top level of the working directory.; Use exactly the filename affiliate_transaction_certification_exhibit.docx.; Do not exceed two rendered pages.; Compare the year ended 31 December 2025 with 2024.; State exactly one certification position: unqualified, qualified, or not supportable.; Do not propose remediation or management action.; Do not invent amounts or include account-level identifiers.; End on the certification decision rather than a next-steps list.)

Nothing outside those filenames is collected. A correct file written anywhere else, or under any other name, scores zero.

WARDENBY UTILITIES
Affiliate-Transaction Compliance Certification Exhibit
Year ended 31 December 2025 | Comparative year ended 31 December 2024
EXECUTIVE CERTIFICATION BASIS
Recorded affiliate transactions increased $1.9 million (8.2%) to $25.0 million in 2025 from $23.1 million in 2024. This exhibit supports one bounded accounting-compliance determination on affiliate transactions and related allocation, reconciliation, review-evidence, and presentation matters; the volume increase is not itself a compliance conclusion.
Management is responsible for the underlying records, allocation practices, and representations. The basis comprises Wardenby’s cost-allocation manual, department records and logs, management representations, and prior-cycle audit findings. Accounting did not independently validate the Engineering allocation model’s design or operating inputs.

Engineering is the largest contributor to the increase ($0.9 million; 47.4% of the total increase), followed by Shared IT ($0.5 million). Engineering’s increase reflects its peak-demand allocation model. The model owner represented that the model was applied consistently; that representation is not an accounting validation of the model’s design or operating inputs. Because those elements were not validated, accounting cannot conclude on that allocation basis. This limitation is consequential given Engineering’s $7.6 million of 2025 affiliate activity.

The logs offset the stale receivable against the stale payable and therefore show the net receivable. Wardenby’s cost-allocation manual prohibits offsetting; the presentation is inconsistent with that internal requirement. Stale status concerns unresolved balances, whereas offsetting concerns their presentation. The substantially larger 2025 gross stale balances make the current-year netting matter more significant than in 2024; arithmetic netting does not settle, extinguish, or validate either gross balance.
RECONCILIATION AND REVIEW-EVIDENCE CONTEXT
The prior-cycle audit found late quarterly reconciliations and missing review evidence. In 2025, quarterly reconciliations were completed on time, an improvement relative to the prior late-reconciliation finding. The Fleet second-quarter review is undated; this is a remaining, narrower exception in evidence of review timing and does not establish that the review was not performed.
CERTIFICATION DECISION
QUALIFIED CERTIFICATION. For the year ended 31 December 2025, the affiliate-transaction compliance certification is qualified for the prohibited netting of stale affiliate balances and the unvalidated Engineering peak-demand allocation-model design and operating inputs, with the undated Fleet second-quarter review noted as an isolated evidence-of-timing gap. The qualification does not negate the recorded transaction totals or the timely 2025 quarterly reconciliations.

spec.professional_context: Lanternwood Supply is providing senior regulatory-accounting support for Wardenby Utilities’ enterprise affiliate-transaction certification. The exhibit will be signed by the controller and read by a commission auditor assessing whether targeted scrutiny is warranted.
difficulty_sources: Selecting one bounded certification position from evidence that supports neither an unqualified conclusion nor total refusal to certify
Separating management representation about an engineering model from conclusions accounting can support
Replacing misleading net presentation with concise gross disclosure under a two-page limit
Comparing periods and identifying material drivers without treating volume changes as compliance findings
Reconciling executive accessibility with the precision expected by a commission auditor
Revising prior overbroad assurance language while keeping the exhibit signature-ready

mode_and_intended_verdict.decision_logic: An unqualified certification is not defensible because the logs use offsetting prohibited by Wardenby’s manual, accounting did not validate the design or operating inputs of the material Engineering allocation model, and one current-year review lacks dated evidence. A wholly unsupported position is too severe because all department totals are available and internally reconcilable, the Engineering model owner represented consistent application, and 2025 quarterly reconciliations were timely. The gold must therefore make one bounded qualified certification and end on that determination.

required_factual_relationships: 2025 department amounts sum to $25.0 million: $7.4 million Customer Operations, $5.8 million Shared IT, $4.2 million Fleet, and $7.6 million Engineering.
2024 department amounts sum to $23.1 million: $7.0 million Customer Operations, $5.3 million Shared IT, $4.1 million Fleet, and $6.7 million Engineering.
The total increase is $1.9 million, approximately 8.2% of the 2024 total.
Department increases are $0.4 million Customer Operations, $0.5 million Shared IT, $0.1 million Fleet, and $0.9 million Engineering.
Engineering is the largest driver and accounts for approximately 47.4% of the total increase.
The 2025 stale balances are a $0.78 million receivable and $0.47 million payable. Their arithmetic net is a $0.31 million receivable, while their gross total is $1.25 million.
The 2024 stale balances are a $0.18 million receivable and $0.085 million payable. Their arithmetic net is a $0.095 million receivable, while their gross total is $0.265 million.
Gross stale balances increased by $0.985 million. The compliance analysis must emphasize gross exposure rather than treating the smaller net residual as the meaningful amount.
imperfections_and_tensions_to_preserve: The logs obscure separate stale receivables and payables through netting, even though the internal manual prohibits offsetting. The gold must disclose both gross sides and identify the manual departure.

Engineering’s model owner represented consistent application, but accounting did not validate either model design or operating inputs. The gold may report the representation but cannot certify technical validity or conclude that the model is wrong.

The prior audit found both late reconciliations and missing review evidence. Current reconciliations are timely, showing improvement, but an undated Fleet second-quarter review leaves a narrower documentation exception.

The executive signer needs an immediately intelligible conclusion, while the commission auditor needs precise basis, scope, gross figures, limitations, and comparative analysis. The gold must provide contextual clarity without becoming a tutorial.

The form expects one certification position, while the available evidence prevents an unqualified assertion but does not invalidate every recorded fact. The explicit trade-off must be resolved through a bounded qualified position.
professional_content_expected: Identify Wardenby Utilities and the year ended 31 December 2025, with 2024 as comparator.
Define the scope narrowly enough to avoid implying broader financial-statement or enterprise-wide regulatory assurance.
Attribute underlying records, allocation operation, and representations to management.
Differentiate transaction volume from outstanding balances.
Present the department comparison compactly and explain the material movement, prioritizing Engineering and Shared IT.
Separate transaction-volume analysis from compliance exceptions; growth is not itself noncompliance.
Describe the peak-demand basis and management representation while stating both unvalidated design and unvalidated operating inputs.
Present stale receivables and payables gross, explain the log net amounts, and identify the internal-manual violation.
Distinguish stale status from prohibited offsetting.
Compare prior audit findings with current-year evidence, recognizing timely reconciliations without overstating closure of the review-evidence issue.
State one qualified certification tied to the netting departure, Engineering validation limitation, and Fleet evidence gap.
Avoid remediation recommendations, audit-opening advice, invented adjustments, invented thresholds, unsupported assurance terminology, and sensitive account-level data.
Provide a controller signature and blank date field, and make the final substantive sentence the certification decision.
must_not_claim: That an audit, review, examination, or other assurance engagement was performed.
That the Engineering peak-demand model was validated, technically correct, fair, or suitable.
That lack of a date proves the Fleet review was not performed.
That netting settles, extinguishes, or validates the gross balances.
That all affiliate transactions are complete, accurate, arm’s-length, prudent, or compliant.
That the prior audit findings automatically remained unresolved in full during 2025.
That Wardenby’s internal prohibition is a universal accounting rule or a jurisdiction-specific legal requirement.
That management should make entries, remediate controls, investigate, escalate, or take another action.
That the commission should or should not open an audit.
build_and_validation: Create a polished DOCX exhibit that renders to no more than two legible pages using standard office libraries and an offline office renderer.
Use a compact period-comparison presentation and concise exception analysis, but do not prescribe a particular layout, number of sections, or column order.
Verify every displayed amount and derivative calculation programmatically.
Inspect the DOCX for comments, tracked changes, placeholders, clipping, and overflow.
Walk all rubric items against the rendered gold and confirm that the single position is consistently qualified wherever it appears.

deliverables.description: A two-page-or-shorter, signature-ready affiliate-transaction compliance certification exhibit comparing 2025 with 2024 and stating one defensible certification position.
constraints: Place the file at the top level of the working directory.
Do not exceed two rendered pages.
Compare the year ended 31 December 2025 with 2024.
State exactly one certification position: unqualified, qualified, or not supportable.
Do not propose remediation or management action.
Do not invent amounts or include account-level identifiers.
End on the certification decision rather than a next-steps list.
